strengths: Novel application of PINNs to continuous-time MARL with theoretically grounded Value Gradient Iteration (VGI) module addressing the practical problem of noisy gradients in PINN-based value learning
Solid theoretical contributions including HJB formulation for multi-agent settings (Lemma 3.1) and convergence guarantee for VGI (Theorem 3.4)

Comprehensive experimental validation with proper ablations consistently demonstrating VGI's importance (Figs. 2-4), design choice analysis (activation functions, loss weighting), and robustness across time intervals
Clear motivation with compelling demonstration (Fig. 1) of why discrete-time methods fail under variable time intervals, well-written presentation
Rigorous experimental methodology including multiple benchmarks and analysis of architectural choices
weaknesses: Severe scope limitation restricting applicability to cooperative multi-agent settings only—cannot handle competitive or mixed-sum games, which are central to much MARL research

Questionable fairness of experimental setup: testing true continuous-time methods against discrete-time baselines on variable-interval environments specifically designed to expose discrete-time weaknesses; missing comparisons with methods that handle variable intervals
Limited technical novelty: primarily applies existing PINN-HJB techniques to MARL; VGI is interesting but relatively incremental as a one-step Bellman backup in gradient space

Insufficient scalability analysis: experiments on small systems (2-4 agents, ≤29D state); PINNs' high-dimensional limitations only partially addressed; claims of 'scaling to complex dynamics' overstated

Theoretical gaps: VGI convergence proof assumes fixed small Δt but training uses uniformly sampled Δt; error propagation from learned dynamics/reward models not analyzed; no convergence guarantee for full algorithm

Model learning inadequately analyzed: separate dynamics/reward model learning introduces errors not thoroughly studied; finite difference discretization ignored; no ablation on joint end-to-end learning
Significant hyperparameter sensitivity without principled selection guidance: Figure 7 shows loss weights heavily impact performance; 'anchor loss' appears ad-hoc lacking theoretical justification
Experimental limitations: only 5 random seeds; large error bars in some results; coupled oscillator limited to linear dynamics; limited baseline comparisons against contemporary methods
Reproducibility concerns: no code availability mentioned; environment modifications for continuous-time variants may be non-trivial; hyperparameter selection process underdocumented
